somerville.name: Somerville Lake
verdict: permit
Limited: waterfowl in marked areas, hogs by permit
Deer hunting is prohibited on Corps land here except on the TPWD WMA (Somerville PHL) and the December challenged-hunter hunt.
rules: Deer
Prohibited at Somerville Lake except the Annual Challenged Hunter Deer Hunt in December (Somerville Lake Office) and the TPWD Wildlife Management Area ((979) 540-6837).
Feral hogs
By permit only: bowhunting, live-trapping, shotgun and dogs, through the Hunt Coordinator at the lake office (compartment drawing).
Waterfowl, daytime public area
Daytime only, inside the yellow markers, never outside the red markers. Hunt from the shoreline. Temporary blinds must be removed when you leave.
Waterfowl, semi-permanent blinds
Assigned for the whole season by random drawing on Recreation.gov.
Closed area
The area near Harge Rd parking lot extending to and across Flag Pond Rd is closed to waterfowl hunting.
All Corps land
Hunter education, a Texas hunting license, and all federal, state and local rules.

belton.name: Belton Lake
verdict: permit
Huntable in designated areas with strict method limits
Shotgun (#2 shot or smaller) and archery only; deer by lottery permit; no turkey.
rules: Legal game
Feral hog, white-tailed deer (permit only), dove, quail, rails, snipe, squirrel, rabbits, waterfowl. Small game and waterfowl Sept 1 – Mar 31 as TPWD allows.
Deer
Archery only, by lottery permit (Recreation.gov 'Belton Lake Archery Deer Hunt Permits' or the lake office).
Feral hog
Archery only, daylight, year-round except during the permitted deer season; no dogs.
Weapons
Archery for hogs and deer; shotguns for everything else. Muzzleloaders, rifles, pistols, slugs and shot larger than #2 are prohibited at all times.
Where
Daylight only in designated areas on the lake maps. No firearms within 600 ft (archery 100 ft) of boundaries, parks, roads, piers, outlets or spillways, or within 600 ft of private property.
Waterfowl
On land only in designated WMAs; on water under TPWD rules and the spacing distances.
Stands and blinds
Portable stands and ground blinds only, no bark penetration; remove at the end of each day.
Hunter orange
400 sq in with orange headgear, 144 sq in front and back (waterfowl hunters exempt once set up).
Prohibited
Turkey, furbearers, predators (bobcat, coyote, lions, raptors), night hunting, spotlighting, trapping, target practice, feeders, electronic calls. Baiting only for permitted deer hunters.
Dogs
Retrieving birds per TPWD; rabbit and squirrel dogs need a lake activity permit, max 6 dogs with GPS collars, handler in orange.
Permits
Hunter education, Texas license and stamps. APH permit not required.
belton.source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers lake hunting page (Fort Worth District Hunting Guide 2026-27)

Sept 1 through the end of goose season.

Blinds
Temporary or natural blinds; remove temporary blinds at the end of each day.
Other

Legal game
Dove, squirrel, rabbits, feral hogs, waterfowl, coyote and deer.
Weapons
Deer, coyote and hogs: archery only (crossbows OK). Birds and small game: non-toxic #2 shot or smaller. No slugs, sabots, #1, B, BB, BBB or buckshot, no rifles, pistols or muzzleloaders.
Seasons
Per the Outdoor Annual for McLennan County. Small game, coyotes and hogs any time except during an open deer season. Deer archery only in every season. No night hunting.
Where
Waterfowl only in the northern and southern zones. No hunting around Waco Wetlands.
Stands and cameras
Portable non-bark-penetrating stands, cameras and ground blinds may stay out if tagged with name, phone and date; tags good 7 days.
Other
Baiting by hand-spreading only. No sport-chasing, no target practice or sighting in. Hog trapping by permit only.
waco.source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers lake hunting page (Fort Worth District Hunting Guide 2026-27)

georgetown.name: Lake Georgetown
verdict: permit
Drawn permits only
Archery deer/hog and small game/waterfowl permits are lottery draws on Recreation.gov.
rules: Permits

Archery deer and hog: apply on Recreation.gov in June ($10 application); if drawn, $100 permit, an archery proficiency test (80%+, IBO course, max 30 yd, dated May 1 or later), hunter education and the mandatory orientation (Aug 15, 2026). Dove, squirrel, rabbits, waterfowl, deer (TPWD MLDP tags) and feral hogs.
Season
Sept 27 - Jan 11 only, within the Williamson County seasons. Everything except archery is closed during archery deer season; all hunting closed from the end of February until dove season.

Deer and hogs archery only; small game and waterfowl shotgun only, non-toxic #2 or smaller. No #1-BBB, buckshot, slugs, rifles, pistols or muzzleloaders.

Hunt Hollow WMA (1,200 ac) for small game and archery permit holders, plus archery-only areas. Walk in from parks and access points; no driving to hunt spots. One location per hunter; no stalking or still hunting.
Stands
Blinds tagged with your permit number, set up only after you get your permit; unmarked blinds are removed.
Other
No night hunting.
georgetown.source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Fort Worth District Public Hunting Guide 2026-27 and the lake's hunting page

Dove, squirrel, rabbits, waterfowl (hunting areas 1-14 only), snipe and feral hog. Deer hunting is illegal on Lavon Corps land until further notice.

grapevine.name: Grapevine Lake

Portable non-bark-penetrating or free-standing stands, removed at the end of each day.
Other
No baiting of any kind, and no varmint calls, baits or lures while hunting (decoys OK). No target shooting, night hunting, trapping or sport chasing.

rules: General

Hunting at Birch Lake is in accordance with applicable federal and state fish and wildlife regulations. Generally, all Corps lands are open to the public for hunting except developed recreational areas and lands around the dam and other structures.
General

Hunters wishing to obtain current hunting regulations or construct duck blinds on Corps lands should reference the current Oklahoma Hunting Guide or contact the Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation, 1801 N. Lincoln Blvd, Oklahoma City, OK 73105 (405) 521-2739.
General
Vehicles may be driven only on established roads and camping is restricted to designated sites.
Restricted hunting areas

As the result of cooperative arrangements between the Oklahoma Wildlife Conservation Commission and the Tulsa District Corps of Engineers, several tracts of Corps lands have been made available to sportsmen for restricted hunting. With the exception of the special restrictions outlined below, all provisions of the Oklahoma Hunting Regulations for Corps of Engineers lands are applicable on these areas.
Restricted hunting areas

As found in the Oklahoma Administrative Code Title 800:25-3-3 (1), the following areas are open for hunting of all species which may legally be taken during legal open seasons by archery equipment only.
1) A 450-acre unit in the Birch Cove, Outlet Park and Twin Cove areas.
